current.text: Brooklyn is projected to start him at forward next to Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe.
Julius Randle joined Brooklyn. He is a ball-dominant player at Porter's position, so Porter will play more at small forward.
Experts expect his usage to drop from last season's 32% because Randle, Brown and Demin will handle the ball more. He may also lose three-point volume. He should still be good.
Josh Minott and Noah Clowney may take some of his minutes.
He becomes an unrestricted free agent next summer and has no contract extension.

A trade during the season is very possible, especially if he and the Nets do not agree on an extension. Slater expects one, possibly within six months. A trade to a team where he gets less usage could drop him to around the 90th best player.
He ended last season with a hamstring injury. Josh sees no major concern going into this season.
Houston owns Brooklyn's pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank. Experts expect little planned rest and maybe more games played than last season.
The Nets also have little reason to win, so his March minutes are uncertain. Young players may get more minutes in the second half of the season.
Brooklyn plays 3-4-3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, with one playoff back-to-back. The Nets have 16 back-to-backs this season, tied for the most in the league.
Josh ranks him 45 to 60 in category leagues. He likes him in the mid rounds and thinks the market has priced in his new situation well. Round 6 is good value.
His ESPN rank of 42 is too high because Randle's arrival makes a repeat of last season unlikely. His worst case without a trade is around 75th.

durable.text: His fantasy value comes from points, many threes and good rebounds. Efficiency and usage drive it. He does not get to the rim much.
Experts say he will never be a real source of assists, steals or blocks.
Threes are his best category, with points next. Both are clearly above the top 250 pool and above other forwards.
He has a long injury history, including a hamstring injury late last season and other injury concerns earlier in his career.

note: He finished about 30th in category leagues last season, but experts now rank him 45 to 60 because Randle cuts his usage. That fits a 10 to 17 USD price, between our league's 10 USD last season and Yahoo's 17 USD value, and he is good value in round 6. He has no flagged weak category, so he fits any build that needs threes and points.
